context.real_world_incident: NoSQL injection vulnerability in MongoDB allowing authentication bypass and unauthorized data access through malicious query operators injected into database queries
context.impact: Approximately 50,000-120,000 records exposed. Attackers can bypass authentication, extract sensitive data, enumerate users, escalate privileges, and in some cases execute arbitrary JavaScript on the database server

references.title: CWE-943: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Query Logic
NoSQL Injection - Testing for NoSQL Injections

conversations.value: Show me an example of NoSQL injection vulnerability in Express.js with MongoDB and how to fix it.
How do I implement production-ready defenses?

exploit_scenario.description: Attacker sends JSON objects with MongoDB query operators ($gt, $ne, $regex, $where) instead of scalar values. A login query like {username: INPUT, password: INPUT} becomes {username: 'admin', password: {$ne: ''}} which matches any non-empty password, bypassing authentication entirely.
preconditions: Application passes parsed JSON body directly to MongoDB queries
No type checking validates that inputs are strings
MongoDB query accepts operator objects in filter fields

secure_properties: All MongoDB query inputs are explicitly cast to expected types (String, Number)
Input validation rejects objects and arrays where scalars are expected
MongoDB queries use projection to limit returned fields
Rate limiting prevents credential stuffing via NoSQL injection
Query timeout prevents $where-based denial of service
negative_properties: Must not pass req.body fields directly to MongoDB find/findOne
Must not allow $-prefixed keys in user input
Must not use $where with user-controlled JavaScript
Must not return full MongoDB documents including _id and internal fields
